about: Confusion pairs (W17). kind: sense (two senses of one headword; a plain headword such as "temper" names its everyday sense, given in the entry's everyday field), lookalike (alike in form or sound, unlike in meaning) or nearmiss (close in meaning, and the SAT sets one against the other). words are library slugs, or plain words that are not library entries. tell is the one line that separates them. Entries' own lookalikes are derived by the build and are not repeated here.

entries.tell: As an adjective, abstract means existing only as an idea; as a noun, an abstract is the short summary printed before a research article.
An apparent flaw may be plain to see or may only seem real; if the passage hints the look misleads (her apparent calm hid panic), it is the seeming sense.
Land or stock that appreciates rises in value, with no object; to appreciate a problem is to grasp how serious it is.
Assets appreciate by rising in price; people appreciate a favor by being grateful for it.
To appreciate the difficulty of a task is to understand it fully, not to be thankful for it.
Assume that something is true and you suppose it without proof; assume a role, a duty or a name and you take it on.
To compromise safety, health or one's principles is to weaken or endanger them; to compromise with a rival is to settle by each side giving ground.
Muscles, metals and economies contract by shrinking; people contract an illness by catching it.
A contract is a signed agreement, but a market or a metal that contracts simply becomes smaller.
To contract measles is to catch it; nothing is signed or agreed.
A curious person is eager to learn; a curious detail or habit is strange. Ask whether the word describes someone's interest or something's oddness.
Defer a decision and you put it off; defer to an expert and you give way to her judgment. The word to marks the yielding sense.
To elaborate on a point (verb) is to add detail; an elaborate plan (adjective) is intricate, with many parts.
People endure hardship by putting up with it; a tradition that endures simply lasts. With an object it is withstand; without one, last.
To grant a request or a license is to give it formally; to grant that a point is true is to admit it before arguing further.
Keen on or keen to means eager; a keen eye, ear or mind is sharp and quick to notice.
Maintain a road or a machine and you keep it in working order; maintain that a claim is true and you insist on it.
A modest person does not boast; a modest gain, budget or house is merely small.
The adjective objective means unbiased and based on facts; the noun an objective is a goal to reach.
The verb obscure means hide or cloud (fog obscured the peak); an obscure poet is little known.
A partial list is incomplete; a partial referee favors one side. Partial to someone also means fond of them.
Peculiar on its own usually means odd; peculiar to means belonging only to, as a plant peculiar to one island.
A prompt reply comes without delay (adjective); to prompt a reply is to cause it (verb).
To qualify a claim is to narrow it with a condition or exception; to qualify for a prize is to meet its requirements.
To render something useless is to make it so; to render a scene, a song or a role is to portray or perform it.
To resolve a dispute (verb) is to settle it; a person's resolve (noun) is firm determination.
To sanction a plan is to approve it officially; sanctions imposed on a country are penalties. The verb usually approves; the plural noun punishes.
To stem a flow is to stop it; to stem from a cause is to arise from it. The word from is the tell.
A field, an experiment or a search yields something by producing it; a person yields to pressure by giving way.
To temper criticism with praise is to soften it; a temper is a tendency to get angry.
To champion a cause is to fight for it; a champion is the winner of a contest.
To arrest a decline or a disease is to halt it; police arrest a suspect by taking him into custody.
A command of a language or a subject is mastery of it; a command is an order to be obeyed.
To check inflation or an advance is to hold it back; to check an answer is to make sure it is right.
A voice that betrays nervousness reveals it without meaning to; betraying a friend is being disloyal.
To entertain an idea or a doubt is to consider it; to entertain guests is to amuse them.
A grave error or threat is very serious; a grave is a burial place.
The verb intimate (IN-tuh-mate) means hint at; the adjective intimate (IN-tuh-mit) means close and personal.
As a verb, to occasion a change is to bring it about; as a noun, an occasion is an event or a time.
Pedestrian prose or ideas are dull and ordinary; a pedestrian is a person traveling on foot.
To reflect on a choice is to think carefully about it; a mirror reflects light.
Reservations about a plan are doubts; a reservation at a hotel is a booking.
A sound argument or method is well reasoned and reliable; a sound is a noise.
Spare prose or decor is plain and lean; a spare key or tire is extra.
To subject samples to heat is to make them undergo it; a subject is a topic or a person under study.
A plan found wanting is lacking or not good enough; wanting a thing is desiring it.
In the wake of an event means in its aftermath; to wake is to stop sleeping.
To advance a theory or an argument is to put it forward; troops advance by moving forward.
To air a grievance or a view is to express it publicly; to air a room is to let fresh air in.
To coin a word or phrase is to invent it; a coin is a piece of metal money.
A request couched in polite terms is phrased that way; a couch is a sofa.
To credit a discovery to someone is to attribute it to that person; to credit an account is to add money to it.
To execute a plan or a design is to carry it out; to execute a prisoner is to put him to death.
To exercise caution, power or a right is to use it; to exercise is to work out.
To fashion a tool out of bone is to shape or make it; fashion is the current style in clothing.
To field questions or complaints is to deal with them as they come; a field is open land.
Interest or energy that flags is weakening; to flag an error is to mark it for attention.
A plan or a ship that founders fails or sinks; a founder is a person who starts an organization.
The gravity of a situation is its seriousness; gravity is also the force that pulls objects toward the ground.
To harbor doubts or a grudge is to hold it privately in mind; a harbor is a port for ships.
To hold that a claim is true is to maintain it; to hold a cup is to grasp it.
Experience that informs an artist's work shapes it; to inform someone is to tell them facts.
A marked change or difference is clearly noticeable; a marked box has a mark written on it.
Minute (my-NOOT) means extremely small; a minute (MIN-it) is sixty seconds.
A moving speech stirs the emotions; a moving train is in motion.
To negotiate a steep trail or an obstacle is to get through it; to negotiate a deal is to bargain.
Critics who pan a film criticize it harshly; a camera that pans sweeps across a scene.
A pressing need or question is urgent; pressing a button is pushing down on it.
To realize a goal or an ambition is to achieve it; to realize a fact is to become aware of it.
To rehearse old arguments or grievances is to repeat or recount them; actors rehearse to practice.
To shoulder a cost or a duty is to take on the burden; to shoulder past someone is to push aside with the body.
In American usage, to table a proposal is to set it aside for later; a table is a piece of furniture.
To tender a resignation or a bid is to offer it formally; tender care is gentle.
To venture a guess or an opinion is to offer it cautiously; a venture is a risky undertaking.
To weather a storm or a crisis is to come through it; rock that has weathered has been worn away by exposure.
A scientific bent is a natural inclination toward science; a bent nail is curved.
A conviction is a firm belief; in court, a conviction is a verdict of guilty.
To discount a rumor or a warning is to treat it as unimportant; to discount a price is to lower it.
A fine distinction is subtle or precise; feeling fine means feeling okay.
A fluid situation is likely to change; a fluid is a liquid or a gas.
To husband resources is to use them sparingly; a husband is a married man.
To mount a campaign or an exhibit is to organize and begin it; to mount a horse is to climb onto it.
A stock phrase or character is standard and predictable; stock is shares in a company or goods kept on hand.
A task that taxes one's patience strains it; a tax is money owed to a government.
A novel's treatment of a theme is the way it handles that theme; medical treatment is care for an illness.
An account of an event is an explanation or a report of it; a bank account is a record of money held.
To conduct a study or a survey is to carry it out; to conduct an orchestra is to lead it.
A cool reception is unfriendly or unenthusiastic; in casual speech, cool means impressive.
A critical step or moment is crucial; a critical review finds fault.
A retiring person is shy and avoids attention; a retiring worker is ending a career.
A scientist's standing is her status or reputation; standing is also being on one's feet.
The verb appropriate (-ate) means take for one's own use, often without permission; the adjective appropriate (-it) means suitable.
An express promise or purpose is clearly stated; an express train makes few stops.
A patent falsehood is obvious; a patent is a legal right to an invention.
The moon waxes as it grows; to wax a floor is to polish it. Wax is the opposite of wane.
Critics who hail a book praise it publicly; to hail a taxi is to call out to it.
Lean years or harvests are meager; to lean on a wall is to rest against it.
Grounds for a complaint are the reasons for it; the ground is the surface of the earth.
In the SAT sense, plastic means easily shaped, as a young brain is plastic; everyday plastic is a synthetic material.
To dwell on a mistake is to keep thinking or talking about it; to dwell in a place is to live there.
A discriminating reader judges quality well; discriminating against people is treating them unfairly.
An arresting image is striking and holds attention; arresting a suspect is taking him into custody.
To act with dispatch is to act with speed and efficiency; to dispatch a messenger is to send him off.
Renege is going back on a promise or deal you made; forsake is abandoning a person, place or belief entirely.
Jettison is throwing out something no longer wanted, such as cargo or a plan; forsake is deserting what you were loyal to.
Rescind is officially canceling a law, rule or offer; renege is failing to keep your own promise.
Theoretical means based on theory rather than practice; hypothetical means supposed for the sake of argument.
Intangible stresses that a thing can't be touched or easily measured, such as goodwill; abstract stresses that it exists as an idea, not a concrete case.
To generalize is to draw a broad rule from particular cases; to extrapolate is to extend a known trend beyond the range actually measured.
Overarching names one idea or goal that ties all the parts together; comprehensive means covering nearly every part.
Adequate is just enough for the purpose; ample is more than enough.
A plethora is an excess, often more than is wanted; myriad simply means countless, with no complaint.
Prolific describes a producer, as an author who writes many books; abundant describes the supply itself.
Acknowledge is to recognize openly, often neutrally; concede is to admit, reluctantly, a point that favors the other side.
Assent is agreeing to a proposal or a statement; concede is admitting, often unwillingly, that the other side is right on a point.
To notice a warning is only to perceive it; to heed it is to pay attention and act on it.
Resigned means accepting what can't be changed without being pleased about it; content means actually satisfied.
Embrace is accepting eagerly; tolerate is putting up with something you may dislike.
Inadvertent means done by accident, without meaning to; spontaneous means done on impulse, meant but unplanned.
Impulsive carries a warning, acting without thinking; spontaneous is usually neutral or approving, unplanned and natural.
Serendipitous is a happy discovery made while looking for something else; fortuitous is anything that happens by chance, now usually lucky chance.
Glean is gathering bit by bit from scattered sources; derive is obtaining from one source, often by reasoning.
You attain a goal or a level by effort; you procure an object or a supply by getting hold of it.
Appropriate is taking for one's own use, often without the right to; procure is obtaining, usually properly.
Vivacious describes a lively, attractive personality; animated describes lively talk or motion at a given moment, as an animated debate.
Dynamic means changing in an energetic, often productive way; volatile means changing unpredictably and dangerously.
Intervene is stepping into a situation to change its course; intercede is stepping in on someone's behalf, to plead for them.
To approach a problem is just to begin taking it up; to grapple with it is to struggle hard with it.
To field questions is to answer them as they come; to deflect them is to turn them aside without answering.
Endorse is publicly approving something another has proposed; espouse is adopting a cause or belief as your own.
Tout is promoting eagerly, often with hype and doubtful claims; advocate is arguing in favor with reasons.
Lobby is pressing officials or lawmakers to act; advocate is arguing for something before any audience.
Propose is putting an idea forward for consideration; advocate is arguing that it should be adopted.
Adapt is changing to suit new conditions; alter is changing in some respect, for any reason.
Overhaul is rebuilding or reforming thoroughly; amend is making a specific change or correction, as to a law.
Amend is making a targeted correction or addition, especially to a law or a document; revise is reworking a whole text after review.
Apprehensive means uneasy about what might happen; distraught means already deeply upset by what has happened.
Trepidation is fearful expectation of what is coming; anticipation is expectation that can be eager.
Onerous is a burden to bear, such as duties or rules; arduous is a task that takes hard, tiring effort, such as a climb.
Daunting stresses that a task discourages the person facing it; formidable can praise, meaning impressively powerful, as a formidable opponent.
Grueling means exhausting to the point of punishment; strenuous means requiring great effort, not necessarily punishing.
Pompous is solemnly self-important in manner or speech; pretentious is trying to seem more cultured or important than one is.
Haughty is proud and aloof toward others; condescending is superior while seeming to stoop kindly toward them.
Pride can be healthy self-respect; hubris is overconfidence that invites a fall.
Allege is claiming without proof, often of wrongdoing; assert is stating firmly, with no hint that the claim is unproven.
Contend is arguing for your own position; concede is admitting a point in favor of the other side.
Proclaim is announcing publicly and formally, to many; assert is stating firmly, in public or not.
Evade is escaping something you ought to face, such as a question or a tax; circumvent is finding a way around a rule or an obstacle.
Abstain is choosing not to take part, especially in a vote or an indulgence; refrain is holding back from an action, as to refrain from comment.
Shun is avoiding a person or group, often to exclude them; eschew is deliberately avoiding a practice or a thing, as to eschew jargon.
Benign means harmless; beneficial means actively helpful.
Salutary is beneficial, often through an unpleasant lesson, as a salutary warning; wholesome is good for health or character in a pleasant way.
Allocate is distributing for a set purpose, as to allocate funds; bestow is giving as an honor.
Endow is providing lasting funds or a quality, as endowed with talent; bestow is presenting a gift or honor on an occasion.
Subjective means shaped by personal views and feelings; partial means unfairly favoring one side.
Tendentious describes writing slanted to push a view; partisan describes a person or group loyal to one side or party.
A bias is any systematic lean, even in data or instruments; a prejudice is an unfair judgment of people formed before knowing them.
Intrepid is fearless and admired; reckless is heedless of danger and blamed.
Audacious is boldly daring, often admired; brazen is shamelessly bold, and blamed for it.
Placid describes a calm temperament or still water, sometimes dull; tranquil describes a peaceful place or state.
Equanimity is calm under strain from someone who still cares; apathy is not caring at all.
Proficient means competent through practice; adept means highly skilled, a step above.
Adroit is skillful and quick in handling things or people; shrewd is sharp in judging what serves one's interest.
Evoke is calling up a memory, image or feeling; elicit is drawing out a response or an answer from someone.
Incite is stirring people up to act, usually violently or unlawfully; provoke is causing a reaction, often anger.
A catalyst triggers or speeds up a change without being the change itself; an impetus is the driving force or motive behind it.
Induce is bringing about or persuading; coerce is forcing by pressure or threats.
Wary is alert to a particular danger; timid is fearful by temperament, lacking courage.
Prudent stresses caution about risk; judicious stresses sound judgment in weighing a choice.
Vigilant is watchful for danger as it comes; circumspect is careful to consider consequences before acting or speaking.
Definitive means final and authoritative, as a definitive study; unequivocal means leaving no doubt about what is meant, as an unequivocal no.
Inevitable means certain to happen sometime; imminent means about to happen soon.
Incontrovertible describes evidence or facts that can't be disputed; unequivocal describes a statement that can't be misread.
Desultory is aimless and halfhearted, lacking purpose; haphazard is random, lacking a plan or an order.
Chaotic stresses total disorder; tumultuous stresses noise and turbulent upheaval.
Articulate is expressing an idea clearly in words; elaborate is adding more detail to an idea already stated.
Delineate is marking out the exact boundaries or features of something; describe is telling what it is like.
Explicate is interpreting a text in detail, line by line; elucidate is making any obscure point clear.
A rationale is the actual reasoning behind a choice; a rationalization is a self-serving excuse invented afterward.
Lucid means clear and easy to understand; coherent means logically connected, so the parts fit together.
Synthesize is combining ideas or sources into something new; integrate is fitting a part into an existing whole.
Coalesce is coming together of its own accord, as droplets or factions do; amalgamate is merging organizations or materials, often by design.
Attribute a result to any cause, good or bad; credit someone with it usually implies praise.
A complement completes or pairs well with something; a supplement adds to what is already complete.
Vie is competing eagerly for something, as to vie for a prize; rival as a verb is matching or equaling, as few cities rival Paris.
Intricate praises fine, complex detail; convoluted faults needless, tangled complexity.
Nuanced means alert to fine distinctions; sophisticated means highly developed, complex or worldly.
Conform is matching accepted norms or standards; comply is obeying a specific rule or request.
Docile describes a quiet, easily led temperament; compliant describes obeying rules or requests, sometimes too readily.
Extensive is large in range or amount; comprehensive is complete, covering nearly everything that matters.
Holistic means treating the whole as more than its parts, looking at how they interact; comprehensive means covering all the parts.
Surreptitious stresses a sneaky act done unnoticed; clandestine stresses an organized secret, as a clandestine meeting.
Furtive describes shifty, guilty-looking behavior, as a furtive glance; covert describes an operation that is officially secret.
Veil is partly hiding or disguising, as a veiled threat; conceal is hiding completely.
Concise is brief and complete, a compliment; terse is brief to the point of rudeness.
Laconic describes a person who uses few words by habit; terse describes a reply cut short, often curtly.
Pithy is brief and full of meaning or wit; succinct is simply brief and clear.
Summarize is restating only the main points, more briefly; paraphrase is restating all of it in other words.
Empirical means drawn from observation or experiment; theoretical means drawn from theory and reasoning.
Specific means particular rather than general; concrete means observable and real rather than abstract.
Tangible means real enough to touch or measure, as tangible results; palpable means so strong it can almost be felt, as palpable tension.
Concur is people agreeing; coincide is events happening at the same time, or things matching.
Consensus is general agreement of nearly everyone; a majority is merely more than half.
Compatible means able to exist together without conflict; consistent means in agreement across cases or with itself.
Blatant stresses that a wrong is done openly, without hiding it; flagrant stresses that it is shockingly serious.
Conspicuous means easy to notice; salient means most important or relevant, standing out as key.
Perpetuate means keep something going; perpetrate means commit a crime or a wrong.
Persevere is admired persistence toward a goal; persist can be neutral or unwelcome, as a cough persists.
Protract means drag out, usually tediously; prolong means make last longer, neutral or welcome.
Abridge is shortening a text while keeping its essentials; truncate is cutting off a part, often abruptly.
Curtail cuts something back or short; curb holds something in check.
Conventional means following usual practice; orthodox means following accepted doctrine, as in religion or a scientific theory.
Reciprocal means given in return, one to the other; mutual means shared by both at once.
Venal means open to bribery; mercenary means motivated chiefly by money.
Nefarious means wicked or criminal in intent; egregious means shockingly bad, as an egregious error, not necessarily wicked.
Concoct is making something up, often a false story; formulate is carefully developing a plan or an idea.
Followed by in or from, originate means begin or come from (the custom originated in Germany); with an object, it means be the first to create (she originated the idea).
Originate is being the first to create, as to originate an idea; generate is producing, as a power plant generates electricity.
Plausible seems reasonable but may be unproven; credible is believable on the evidence.
Tenable means able to be defended against attack; valid means logically sound.
Disparage is belittling, calling something unimportant or poor; deride is mocking it with open contempt.
Criticize is pointing out faults; condemn is the strongest, declaring something wrong.
Dismissive treats something as not worth attention; disdainful looks down on it as beneath one.
Derisive means mocking; derisory means so small it is laughable, as a derisory offer.
Callous is unfeeling toward others' suffering; ruthless is pitiless in pursuing a goal.
Vindictive seeks revenge for a wrong; spiteful wants to hurt or annoy with no wrong required.
Malicious describes an act meant to harm; malevolent describes a wish or a nature bent on harm.
A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one; a pretense is a false show, as a pretense of interest.
Evasive describes a person dodging a question on purpose; elusive describes something hard to find, catch or grasp.
Disingenuous is pretending to be more innocent or less informed than one is; hypocritical is claiming standards one does not follow.
Devious is sneaky and indirect in getting one's way; duplicitous is two-faced, saying one thing and doing another.
Falter is losing strength or momentum, perhaps briefly; flounder is struggling clumsily, as if stuck.
Stagnate is ceasing to grow or move; languish is weakening or suffering from neglect over time.
Wane is gradual weakening after a peak, as the moon or influence wanes; dwindle is shrinking in number or size, as savings dwindle.
Erode is wearing away gradually by friction or pressure; dissipate is scattering and vanishing, or wasting.
Infringe is violating a right or rule by encroaching on it, as on a patent; transgress is crossing a moral or legal limit.
Contravene is going against a rule or law, even unknowingly; flout is disregarding it openly and scornfully.
Belated describes something that comes too late, as belated thanks; tardy describes a person slow to arrive or act.
Procrastinate is putting off from reluctance or habit; defer is postponing by decision, often for good reason.
Deliberate means done intentionally after thought; willful adds stubborn defiance, as willful disobedience.
Premeditated is planned well in advance, usually of a crime; deliberate is intentional, whether or not planned far ahead.
Characterize is naming something's essential nature, as characterizing a speech as cautious; describe is telling what it is like in detail.
Outline is laying out the main points and how they are organized; summarize is condensing the content into a brief statement.
Revoke is canceling a right or a license granted to someone; rescind is canceling a law, an order or a decision.
Confiscate is seizing by legal authority; appropriate is taking for one's own use, often without the right to.
Withhold is refusing to give what is expected; deprive is taking away or denying what someone needs.
Abolish is formally ending a practice or an institution, as slavery; eradicate is wiping something out completely, as a disease.
Distinct means clearly separate or definite; distinctive means characteristic, marking something off from others.
Juxtapose is placing things side by side; contrast is showing how they differ, which juxtaposing may or may not do.
Divergent means moving apart from a common point, as divergent paths; disparate means fundamentally different from the start.
Dissuade is talking someone out of an action; deter is discouraging it, often through fear of consequences.
Embellish is adding decorative or exaggerated details to a true account; falsify is altering facts or records to make them false.
Skew is biasing results in one direction; distort is twisting something out of its true shape or meaning.
Diverse describes a varied group; eclectic describes a taste or method that draws from many sources.
Prevailing means currently dominant, as the prevailing view; prevalent means widespread, as a prevalent disease.
Understate is presenting something as less than it is; minimize can also mean actually reduce, as minimizing costs.
Ostensible means stated or apparent, the given reason perhaps hiding another; purported means claimed but not proven, as a purported letter.
Implausible means hard to believe; untenable means impossible to defend once challenged.
Banal is dull because unoriginal and overused; mundane is simply ordinary and everyday, not necessarily dull.
Tedious is tiresome because long or slow; monotonous is dull because unchanging.
Zealous is intensely devoted, often admired; fanatical is devoted beyond reason.
Fledgling describes a new venture or group just starting out; a novice is a person who is a beginner.
Emphasize is stressing what is true; overstate is claiming more than is true.
Dwell on is lingering, often too long, as dwelling on a mistake; focus on is directing attention, a neutral act.
Galvanize is jolting people suddenly into action; stimulate is spurring activity or growth, often gradually.
Foster is encouraging something to develop, as fostering debate; nurture adds ongoing care, as a parent nurtures a child.
An incentive is an outside reward that encourages action; a motive is the inner reason a person acts.
Menace is threatening with harm, often by presence or intent; jeopardize is putting something at risk of loss or failure.
Perennial means recurring year after year; perpetual means never stopping.
Abiding is lasting and steady, usually of a good feeling, as an abiding faith; chronic is long-lasting and recurring, usually of a problem.
Intrigued is curious and interested; rapt is completely absorbed, attention fixed.
Innate is inborn in a living being, as innate talent; inherent is built into anything, as the risks inherent in a plan.
Integral means forming an essential part of a whole; indispensable means impossible to do without.
Requisite means required; a prerequisite is required beforehand, as a course that must come first.
Legal means allowed by law; legitimate means rightful or justified, by law or by reason, as a legitimate concern.
Peruse traditionally means read carefully and thoroughly; skim means glance through quickly.
Analyze is examining the parts to see how they work; assess is judging value, quality or size after examining.
Ascertain is finding out for certain; assume is taking as true without checking.
Disseminate is spreading information widely on purpose; permeate is spreading through every part of something, as a smell permeates a room.
Explicit is stated outright; implicit is suggested but not stated.
Abet is helping along a wrongdoing; facilitate is making any task easier, usually a good one.
Facilitate is making a process easier; expedite is making it faster.
Erroneous means simply wrong, as an erroneous date; fallacious means resting on faulty reasoning, as a fallacious argument.
Counterfeit is a fake copy made to pass as the real thing, as counterfeit money; fabricated is invented outright, as fabricated evidence.
Illusory means seeming real but not; allusive means full of indirect references to other works.
Elusive means hard to catch or pin down; allusive means hinting at or referring to other works.
Vacillate is going back and forth between choices; waver is becoming unsteady or hesitant, in resolve or in motion.
Malleable means easily shaped or influenced by others; versatile means able to do many things well.
Conclude is simply ending; culminate is ending at a final high point.
Cordial is warmly polite, often formal; affable is easygoing and easy to talk to.
Amicable describes a relationship or settlement free of conflict, as an amicable parting; cordial describes warm, polite manners.
Frugal is careful with money, a virtue; parsimonious is stingy to a fault.
Futile efforts achieve nothing; counterproductive efforts make things worse.
Lavish is generous or costly in the extreme, often admiringly; extravagant stresses waste, spending beyond reason.
Nostalgic is longing specifically for the past; wistful is a vague, sad longing for anything out of reach.
Bleak means offering little hope now; ominous means warning of trouble to come.
Gradual means happening little by little; glacial means extremely slow, usually as a complaint.
Incremental is steady progress in small steps; piecemeal is bit by bit without an overall plan, often a criticism.
Insidious stresses harm that creeps in unnoticed; pernicious stresses harm that is deadly or ruinous, often hidden.
Impede is slowing progress; obstruct is blocking it, partly or wholly.
Encumber is weighing down with a burden, as encumbered by debt; hamper is getting in the way of movement or progress.
Interrupt is breaking into something briefly; disrupt is throwing its normal course into disorder.
Stymie is blocking progress so that one is stuck; thwart is defeating a plan outright.
Candid is frank by choice; ingenuous is innocently open, often from inexperience.
Veracity is truthfulness, of a person or a report; validity is logical soundness, of an argument.
Auspicious is a good sign at the start, as an auspicious beginning; propitious is conditions favorable for success, as propitious weather.
Optimistic is generally expecting good outcomes; sanguine is calmly confident even when things look bad.
Buoyant is cheerfully resilient, bouncing back; exuberant is overflowing with lively joy.
Belligerent describes a nation at war or a person openly aggressive; pugnacious describes a temperament eager to fight or argue.
Deferential is respectfully yielding to another's judgment; servile is fawningly obedient, a fault.
Modest is not boasting; self-effacing goes further, keeping oneself out of the spotlight.
Idealistic is guided by high ideals; quixotic is idealistic to the point of being foolishly impractical.
Visionary praises bold, imaginative foresight; utopian suggests an ideal too perfect to be realized.
Uninformed is lacking the facts; naive is too trusting from lack of experience.
Imply is suggesting without stating, a neutral act; insinuate is slyly hinting at something unpleasant.
Allude is referring indirectly to a person, work or event; imply is suggesting an idea without stating it.
Tacit is understood without being spoken, as tacit approval; implicit is contained in what is said without being stated outright.
Pivotal is a turning point on which the outcome depends; fundamental is basic, what everything else rests on.
Seminal describes a work that strongly influenced later work; pioneering describes being first to try something.
Paramount means of top importance; prominent means easily seen or widely known.
Rectify is correcting an error or a fault; redress is setting right a wrong done to someone, often with compensation.
Ameliorate is making a bad situation better; mitigate is making something harmful less severe.
Chronicle is recording events in the order they happened; document is recording with evidence.
Paradoxical is seemingly self-contradictory yet possibly true; contradictory is asserting two things that can't both be true.
Incongruous is strikingly out of place in its setting; inconsistent is not agreeing with itself or with other facts.
Burgeon is growing or flourishing rapidly; proliferate is multiplying rapidly in number.
Augment is adding to something to enlarge it; escalate is growing rapidly more intense or serious, as a conflict escalates.
Indifferent is not caring about a particular matter; apathetic is lacking interest or concern in general.
Blasé is unimpressed from overfamiliarity; jaded adds weariness from having had too much.
Detached is emotionally uninvolved, sometimes coldly; dispassionate is calm and fair, unswayed by emotion.
Callow is young and inexperienced, often immature; naive is too trusting, at any age.
Mediocre is only average; subpar is below the expected standard.
Strident is loud and harsh in sound or tone; vehement is forceful and passionate in feeling.
Acute is intense and sudden, as acute pain; severe is harsh or grave in degree, however it arrives.
Amplify is making something stronger or louder, a neutral act; exacerbate is making a problem worse.
Exacerbate means make a problem worse; exasperate means annoy a person intensely.
Arbitrary is based on choice or chance rather than reason; capricious is changing suddenly on a whim.
Irrelevant is unrelated to the point; extraneous is added from outside and not needed.
Magnanimous is generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival; altruistic is selflessly concerned for others' welfare.
Erudite is deeply learned, of a person; scholarly describes careful academic work or manner.
Muted is softened in color, sound or reaction, as muted applause; understated is deliberately restrained in style.
Allay is putting a fear or a doubt to rest; assuage is easing a feeling, such as grief or guilt, or satisfying a hunger.
Mollify is soothing someone's anger; placate is calming someone by giving in a little.
Alleviate is relieving pain or hardship that people feel; mitigate is reducing the severity of something harmful, as a risk or a penalty.
Measured is careful and deliberate, as a measured response; restrained is holding back feeling or force.
Ingenious is cleverly inventive in solving a problem; innovative is introducing new methods or ideas.
Radical is fundamental, going to the root of something; drastic is extreme and sudden in effect.
Neutral takes no side at all; impartial may judge between sides but favors neither.
Equal gives everyone the same; equitable gives everyone what is fair, which may differ.
Ambiguous has two or more possible meanings; vague has no clear meaning at all.
Cryptic is deliberately hard to decode, as a cryptic note; enigmatic is mysterious and hard to read, often of a person.
Redact is blacking out parts of a document so they can't be read; excise is cutting a passage or part out entirely.
Omit means leave out; emit means send out, as light, heat or gas.
Dissent is disagreeing with the majority or an official view; oppose is acting or arguing against something.
Structured is organized by a clear plan; regimented is strictly controlled, often too strictly.
Ornate is heavily decorated; opulent is lavishly rich and luxurious.
Outspoken is frank in stating opinions; vociferous is loud and insistent about them.
Overlook is missing something by accident; disregard is ignoring it on purpose.
Sketchy is lacking detail, rough; fragmentary is surviving only in broken pieces, as a fragmentary manuscript.
Passive is acted on rather than acting, by nature or by choice; inert is not moving or reacting at all, as an inert gas.
Coax is gentle, patient urging; cajole adds flattery or repeated pleading.
Cogent is convincing because clear and logical; persuasive is convincing by any means, including emotion.
Spartan stresses bare living without comforts; austere stresses severe plainness or sternness in style or manner.
Facetious is joking about something serious when joking is out of place; flippant is lightly disrespectful.
Wry is dry, mildly mocking humor; sardonic is grimly scornful mockery.
Ironic is saying the opposite of what is meant, or an outcome opposite to what was expected; sarcastic is using irony to mock or wound.
Alienate is pushing people away, as supporters; estrange is making those once close into strangers, as estranged siblings.
Pragmatic is practical and results-minded, usually approving; expedient is convenient at the cost of principle.
Feasible means possible to carry out; viable means able to succeed or survive once done.
Admire is regarding with approval; revere is deep, almost sacred respect.
Commend is praising formally, often for a specific act; laud is praising highly and publicly.
Reverent means deeply respectful; a reverend is a member of the clergy.
A harbinger is a sign announcing what is coming, as a harbinger of spring; a precursor is an earlier form that led to a later one.
A precedent is an earlier case that serves as a model; precedence is priority in order or rank.
Predict is saying what will happen; anticipate is expecting it and often preparing for it.
A person predicts; a sign or an event presages, foreshadowing what is to come.
Conserve is using sparingly to avoid waste, as conserving water; preserve is keeping something intact and safe from harm or decay.
Forestall is heading something off by acting early; preclude is ruling it out entirely in advance.
Obviate is making something unnecessary, as a new bridge obviates the ferry; preclude is making it impossible.
Avert is preventing something bad from happening, as averting a crisis; avoid is keeping away from it.
Neutralize is canceling an effect entirely; offset is balancing it with an opposite effect, perhaps only in part.
Safeguard is protecting with a measure or a rule; fortify is strengthening against attack.
Aspire is hoping and aiming to achieve something; pursue is actively working toward it.
Intermittent is stopping and starting at intervals, as intermittent rain; sporadic is scattered and irregular, occurring now and then.
Rational means based on logic; reasonable adds fair and moderate, as a reasonable price.
Appease is giving in to demands to keep the peace, often a criticism; placate is calming someone's anger, often with a small concession.
Mediate is helping two sides reach their own agreement; arbitrate is deciding the dispute for them.
Resolve is settling a dispute or a problem; reconcile is making two things fit together, or restoring a friendship.
Disavow is denying any connection to something; repudiate is rejecting it firmly and publicly.
Rebuff is rejecting bluntly; spurn is rejecting with contempt.
Reject is refusing to accept; dismiss adds treating the thing as not worth consideration.
Forfeit is losing something as a penalty; cede is giving it up, usually by agreement or under pressure.
Relinquish is giving up something held, often reluctantly; renounce is formally declaring that one gives it up or rejects it.
Forgo is choosing to go without; forfeit is losing through a penalty or a failure.
Hesitant is slow to act from uncertainty; reluctant is unwilling, though one may still act.
Grudging describes what is given unwillingly, as grudging respect; reluctant describes the unwilling person.
Renowned is famous and admired; notorious is famous for something bad.
Reticent is reluctant to share feelings or information on a matter; taciturn is habitually silent.
Aloof is cool and distant in company; reclusive is keeping away from company altogether.
Constrain is limiting the choices available; restrain is holding back an action or a person.
Stringent describes strict rules or standards; rigorous describes thorough, exacting work.
To qualify a claim is to accept it within limits; to undermine it is to weaken its support.
Disclose is making known, often formally, as disclosing a conflict of interest; divulge is revealing a secret or private matter.
Divulge is revealing on purpose; betray is revealing without meaning to, as a trembling hand betrays fear.
Robust is strong enough not to break; resilient is able to recover after being bent or damaged.
Sparse is thinly spread over an area; meager is too little in amount.
Isolate is setting one thing apart, as to study it; segregate is keeping groups apart, often by policy.
Solemn is grave and dignified, as a solemn vow; somber is gloomy and dark in mood or color.
Earnest is sincere and serious in intent; solemn is formal and grave in manner.
Imitate is copying; emulate is copying in order to match or surpass, usually someone admired.
Simplistic oversimplifies a complex matter; facile adds glib ease, reached too easily to be trusted.
Rudimentary is basic because undeveloped, as a rudimentary tool; simplistic is simple because it ignores complexity, a criticism.
Skeptical is doubtful until shown proof; incredulous is unable to believe what one has just seen or heard.
Negligible is too small to matter; nominal is small and in name only, as a nominal fee.
Modest is small without complaint; paltry is insultingly small.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation to be tested; a theory is an explanation that has survived much testing.
Infer is concluding from evidence; surmise is guessing from little evidence.
Hypothesize is proposing a testable explanation; speculate is guessing without firm evidence.
Stable is steady, usually a good thing; stagnant is not moving or developing, usually a bad thing.
Desist is stopping an action, often on demand, as in cease and desist; discontinue is ending a service, a product or a practice.
Resolute is firmly determined, admired; obstinate is stubbornly unwilling to change, blamed.
Dogmatic is insisting one's beliefs are right without evidence; intransigent is refusing to compromise in a dispute.
Reliant is depending on support from someone or something; contingent is depending on a condition being met.
Ancillary is supporting but secondary, as ancillary services; subordinate is ranked below in a hierarchy.
Appreciable is just large enough to notice or measure; substantial is large.
Dormant is inactive for now but able to wake, as a dormant volcano; latent is present but not yet shown, as latent talent.
Subtle is hard to notice but noticeable with care; imperceptible cannot be noticed at all.
Abrupt is sudden and unexpected, as an abrupt ending; precipitous is steep and sudden, as a precipitous drop in prices.
Meteoric describes a very fast rise; precipitous usually describes a steep fall.
Cursory is quick and not thorough, as a cursory glance; perfunctory is done merely as routine, without interest or care.
Lax is not strict enough, as lax security; negligent is failing in a duty of care, which can cause harm.
Superfluous is more than is needed; gratuitous is uncalled for, often offensively so.
Redundant is unnecessary because it repeats something already there; superfluous is unnecessary in any way.
Surpass is doing better than a rival or a record; transcend is rising above a limit altogether, as art that transcends its era.
Surpass is merely doing better; eclipse is surpassing so completely that the other is overshadowed.
Corroborate is confirming with an independent source; substantiate is backing up a claim with evidence of any kind.
Indicate is pointing to something fairly directly; suggest is pointing to it more tentatively.
Justify is giving good reasons for; vindicate is proving right after doubt or blame.
Quell is putting down unrest or calming a fear; quash is crushing, or legally canceling, as quashing a verdict.
Unforeseen is not expected ahead of time, however mild; startling is shocking in the moment.
Diligent is steadily hardworking; meticulous is extremely careful about detail.
Meticulous is careful about detail; scrupulous adds careful honesty, doing what is right.
Affluent describes people or places that are wealthy; lucrative describes an activity that makes a lot of money.
Expeditious is quick and efficient; hasty is quick and careless.
Ephemeral lasts only a very short time by nature, as a mayfly; transient passes through and does not stay, as a transient population.
Trivial is of little importance; frivolous adds silliness, not serious when seriousness is called for.
Incidental is occurring alongside something as a minor side effect; peripheral is at the edge, away from the center of attention.
Accurate is free of error; faithful is true to an original, as a faithful translation.
Authentic means genuinely what it claims to be; veritable is an intensifier meaning truly deserving the name, as a veritable flood.
Exemplify is being a typical example; epitomize is being the perfect example.
Illustrate is making clear by example; embody is giving an idea visible form, as a person embodies courage.
Equivocal describes a statement open to more than one reading; ambivalent describes a person with mixed feelings.
Deduce is reasoning from general rules to a conclusion that must follow; infer is concluding from evidence, likely but not certain.
Perceive is noticing or understanding; discern is perceiving a fine difference or something hard to see.
Standardized is made to fit one set pattern by design; homogeneous is the same throughout by nature.
Anonymous means the name is unknown or withheld; obscure means little known at all.
Idiosyncratic is distinctively one's own, as an idiosyncratic style; eccentric is odd enough to depart from what is normal.
An anomaly breaks an expected pattern and invites explanation; an aberration departs from what is normal or right, often a lapse.
Harness is putting a force to productive use, as harnessing wind; exploit is using for gain, often unfairly.
Evocative calls up images, memories or feelings; poignant is sharply and sadly moving.
Capricious is acting on sudden whims; mercurial is changing moods quickly and unpredictably.
Erratic is irregular and unpredictable in pattern; volatile is liable to change suddenly and explosively.
Tenuous is weak or thin, as a tenuous connection; precarious is dangerously unstable, liable to fall.
Vulnerable is open to harm or attack; susceptible is easily affected or influenced, as susceptible to colds.
Brittle is hard but easily snapped; frail is weak and delicate.
Fritter is wasting little by little, as frittering away an afternoon; squander is wasting carelessly, often on a large scale.
Refute is proving a claim false; discredit is damaging trust in a claim or a person, without necessarily disproving it.
Dispel is driving away a belief or a fear; refute is proving an argument false.
Prevalent is widespread; endemic is regularly found in a particular place or group, as a disease endemic to a region.
Ubiquitous is seemingly everywhere at once; pervasive is spreading through every part of something, as a pervasive smell.
Prevalent is widespread; rampant is spreading unchecked, usually of something bad.
Garrulous describes a person who talks too much, often about trivial things; verbose describes speech or writing with too many words.
Verbose uses more words than needed; rambling also wanders from the point.
Regress is going back to an earlier, worse state; relapse is falling back into an illness or a habit after improving.
Deteriorate is getting worse on its own; debilitate is weakening someone or something severely.
Conceptual concerns ideas and how they are framed, as a conceptual model; theoretical concerns theory as opposed to practice or testing.
Numerous counts separate things, as numerous errors; ample measures a supply, as ample time.
Sufficient is about quantity, enough of it; adequate is also about quality, good enough but no better.
Spirited is lively and determined in attitude, as a spirited defense; vigorous is strong and energetic in action, as vigorous exercise.
Proactive is acting early in general to prevent problems; preemptive is striking first against a specific expected threat.
A proponent argues publicly for an idea; an adherent is a follower who holds it.
Revamp is renovating to improve appearance or appeal; overhaul is thoroughly examining and rebuilding how something works.
Perturbed is unsettled and worried; distraught is so upset one can hardly function.
Arrogant is a general air of superiority; presumptuous is a specific act of overstepping, as a presumptuous request.
Affirm is stating that something is true; argue is giving reasons to show that it is.
Advantageous gives an edge or a benefit to someone; constructive is aimed at improving something, as constructive criticism.
Confer can mean consult, as conferring with colleagues, but to confer a degree or an honor is to grant it.
One-sided leaves out the other side; tendentious is actively slanted to promote a cause.
Rash is acting hastily without weighing risk; impetuous adds sudden, emotional force.
Serene is untroubled calm, often of a place or a face; composed is calm kept by self-control under pressure.
A factor is one of several contributing elements; a catalyst is what triggers the change.
To influence an outcome is to be one push among others; to determine it is to fix it.
Caution is care to avoid danger or error; a caveat is a specific warning or qualification attached to a claim.
Ensure is making sure something happens; guarantee adds a formal promise that it will.
Disorderly is unruly, as disorderly conduct; disorganized is badly planned or arranged.
Clarify is making something easier to understand; simplify is making it less complex, which can lose detail.
Explain is telling how or why; illuminate is shedding new light, revealing what was not seen before.
Hybrid is one thing formed from two kinds, as a hybrid plant; heterogeneous is a mix of unlike parts that stay distinct.
Labyrinthine is maze-like, hard to find a way through; convoluted is twisted and needlessly complicated.
Complex is made of many connected parts; intricate stresses fine, delicate detail.
Abide by is accepting and obeying a rule or a decision; adhere to is sticking closely to it over time.
Comprehensive describes full coverage of one subject; encyclopedic describes vast knowledge across many subjects.
Inclusive stresses leaving no one out, as an inclusive policy; comprehensive stresses covering every part of a subject.
Harmonious is fitting together pleasingly; congruent is matching or agreeing, as findings congruent with a theory.
Evident is clear from the evidence; apparent can mean only seeming, so evident is the safer word for what is shown.
Stark is harsh and unmistakable, as a stark contrast; blatant is openly obvious, usually of wrongdoing.
Prolong is making something last longer than it otherwise would; sustain is keeping it going at its level, often by supplying what it needs.
Linger is staying on or being slow to fade, as a smell lingers; persist is continuing despite opposition or difficulty.
Compress is squeezing into less space; condense is shortening a text while keeping its main points.
Effortless means needing no effort, often thanks to skill, as an effortless performance; undemanding means the task itself asks little.
Manageable means able to be handled or controlled; feasible means able to be done at all.
Archaic belongs to a much earlier time, as archaic spelling; outmoded is simply out of date, recently passed by.
Obsolete is already out of use; obsolescent is on its way to becoming obsolete.
A stock phrase is standard and predictable; a hackneyed one is so overused that it has gone stale.
Trite is stale from overuse; trivial is unimportant.
Cooperate is going along with or helping; collaborate is working together to produce something.
Concerted describes effort made jointly and with determination; synergy is the extra effect when combined parts do more than they would apart.
Unscrupulous describes a person without moral principles; reprehensible describes an act that deserves blame.
Illegal is against the law; illicit also covers what custom or morals forbid, often done in secret.
Construct is building from parts, as constructing an argument; formulate is putting a plan or an idea into precise terms.
Reputable means well regarded and trustworthy in general; authoritative means reliable because it comes from an expert source.
Credulous believes too easily; unquestioning accepts without asking, as unquestioning loyalty.
Naive is innocent from inexperience; gullible is easily fooled into believing false things.
Derisive is mocking out loud, as derisive laughter; contemptuous is showing scorn by any means, even silence.
Mock can be light teasing or imitation; ridicule is harsher, making someone an object of scorn.
Wither is shriveling and losing freshness, as plants or hopes do; atrophy is wasting away from disuse, as a muscle does.
Abate is used of force or intensity, as the wind abated; subside adds sinking back down, as floodwaters subsided.
Diminish is becoming or making smaller; belittle is making something seem smaller or less worthy than it is.
A breach (noun) is a violation of a rule, a trust or an agreement; to rupture (verb) is to burst or break apart suddenly, as a pipe or a friendship does.
Resolute is firmly determined; defiant is boldly refusing to obey.
Tardy is late; dilatory is slow in a way that causes delay, often by habit.
Deliberate is done on purpose after thought; purposeful is showing determination toward a goal.
Depict is showing in words or images; portray adds a particular slant, as portrayed as a villain.
Recount means tell the story of; recant means take back a statement one made.
Deprive is taking away what someone needs; divest is stripping someone of property or power, or selling off holdings.
Eliminate is removing, as from a list or a contest; obliterate is destroying so completely that no trace remains.
Raze is tearing a building down to the ground; erase is rubbing out marks or records.
Discourage is making someone less willing to act; daunt is intimidating them with the size or difficulty of a task.
Warn is telling of a danger ahead; admonish is warning or scolding someone for a fault.
Misrepresent is giving a false or misleading picture; falsify is altering documents or data to make them false.
A caricature exaggerates a subject's features to mock them; a parody imitates a work's style to mock it.
Diverse praises the variety in a group; heterogeneous is a neutral, technical word for being made of unlike parts.
Multifaceted describes a thing or a person with many sides; versatile describes a person able to do many different things.
Autonomous is self-governing, making its own decisions; self-sufficient is providing for its own needs.
Dominant is having the most power or influence; predominant is being the main or most common part.
Dominant simply means strongest now; hegemony is lasting dominance of one state or group over others, often through influence as well as force.
Downplay is making something seem less important than it is; dismiss is refusing to consider it at all.
Questionable is open to question; dubious is more strongly suspect, often of someone's honesty.
Plausible seems reasonable and may be true; specious seems reasonable but is false.
Insipid is bland and flavorless, lacking any interest; prosaic is dull because ordinary and unimaginative.
Fervent is intense feeling for something, as fervent hope; vehement is forceful expression, often against something.
Enthusiastic is eagerly interested; avid is eager and habitual, as an avid reader.
Ardent is warm, passionate devotion, as an ardent admirer; fervent is burning intensity of belief or hope, as a fervent prayer.
Emphatic is forceful and definite; impassioned is full of strong feeling.
Potent is powerful, as a potent drug; efficacious is producing the intended result, which a mild remedy can also do.
Fruitful is producing good results, as a fruitful discussion; prolific is producing a great quantity.
Incipient is just beginning to appear, often of a problem, as an incipient crisis; nascent is just coming into being and starting to develop, as a nascent industry.
Budding is just starting and showing promise, as a budding scientist; embryonic is at a very early, undeveloped stage, as an embryonic plan.
Reiterate is saying again; underscore is stressing importance, which need not involve repeating.
Highlight is pointing attention to something; accentuate is making a feature more noticeable, as lighting accentuates texture.
Exaggerate is making something seem bigger than it is; embellish is adding details, often untrue, to make a story more interesting.
Nourish is feeding growth with what it needs; cultivate is developing something through sustained effort, as cultivating a skill.
Further is helping a goal or a cause advance; promote is also publicizing it, as promoting a product.
Stimulate is spurring activity; invigorate is filling with fresh energy and strength.
Jeopardize is putting something at risk of loss or failure, as jeopardizing a career; imperil is putting in danger, as imperiled species.
Permanent is lasting indefinitely; indelible is permanent because it can't be erased, as ink or a memory.
Riveting describes what holds attention; engrossed describes the person whose attention is held.
Curious is wanting to know; inquisitive is actively asking questions, sometimes intrusively.
Entail is necessarily involving as a consequence, as the job entails travel; imply is suggesting without stating.
Vital is essential to life or continued existence; crucial is decisive for an outcome.
Deep-rooted is firmly established over a long time, as a deep-rooted belief; entrenched adds hard to dislodge, often a criticism, as entrenched interests.
Veteran stresses long service, as a veteran teacher; seasoned stresses skill toughened by experience.
Venerable is respected for age and long service; illustrious is famous for distinguished achievement.
Principled acts by firm moral rules; virtuous is morally good in character.
Integrity is honesty and moral consistency; probity is strict, proven honesty, especially with money or public duty.
Ponder is turning a question over carefully; contemplate can also mean considering a possible action, as contemplating retirement.
Appraise is judging worth or value; critique is analyzing a work's strengths and weaknesses in detail.
Deem is judging to be, formally, as deemed unsafe; consider can also mean simply think about.
Evaluate is judging worth using criteria; scrutinize is examining very closely, looking for flaws.
Probe is investigating closely to uncover facts; trace is following something's development or course back to its origin.
Reflective is thoughtful, often looking back; pensive is quietly thoughtful with a hint of sadness.
Undue is more than is warranted or appropriate, as undue pressure; inordinate is far beyond normal amounts, as an inordinate amount of time.
Exorbitant describes a price or a demand that is unreasonably high; extravagant describes spending or style that is wasteful.
Immoderate is beyond reasonable limits, as immoderate drinking; overwrought is overly agitated, or overdone in style.
Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for effect, not meant literally; to exaggerate may be meant to mislead.
Broaden is widening scope, as broadening a study; extend is lengthening reach or duration, as extending a deadline.
Propagate is spreading an idea, or breeding plants and animals; disseminate is scattering information widely.
Diffuse is spreading out thinly from a source; permeate is filling every part.
Denote is what a word or sign literally means; imply is what a speaker suggests beyond it.
Specify is naming exactly; stipulate is requiring as a condition, as a contract stipulates payment.
Explicit is stated outright; unambiguous is open to only one reading, stated or not.
Enable is making something possible at all; facilitate is making it easier.
Catalyze is sparking a change or speeding one up; expedite is speeding up a process already under way.
Simplify is making less complicated; streamline is making simpler in order to work more efficiently.
Spurious is false though it looks valid, as a spurious correlation; counterfeit is a fake made to deceive, as counterfeit coins.
Pliant is easily bent, often of a person easily influenced; malleable is easily shaped, as metal or opinion.
Subsequent means coming later; consecutive means following one after another without a break.
Contingent depends on something that may happen; consequent results from something that did.
Eventual is happening at some later time; ultimate is final, or the most basic or greatest.
Ensue is following as a result; culminate is ending at a high point.
Amiable describes a good-natured person; congenial describes a person or a setting that suits one pleasantly, as congenial surroundings.
Genial is warm and cheerful; gregarious is fond of company and seeks it out.
Thrifty describes a person careful with money; economical describes a thing or method that saves money or resources.
Frugal is careful spending, a virtue; stingy is unwillingness to spend or share, a fault.
Ineffectual describes a person or measure that fails to have the intended effect; futile describes an effort that could never succeed.
Lavish is generous in the extreme, often admiringly; profligate is recklessly wasteful, and always blamed.
Munificent describes the giver as extremely generous; largesse is the generous giving itself.
Mourn is grieving for a death or a loss; lament is expressing grief or regret aloud.
Pessimistic expects bad outcomes; cynical distrusts people's motives.
Melancholy is a deep, quiet sadness in a person or a mood; somber is gloomy seriousness in tone or color.
Bleak is offering little hope; dismal is gloomy and depressing, or very poor, as a dismal performance.
Adverse is unfavorable, as adverse conditions; detrimental is actually causing harm.
Deleterious is harmful in its effects, often subtly, as deleterious to health; noxious is poisonous or offensive, as noxious fumes.
Hinder is making progress harder; inhibit is holding back a process or a feeling, often from within.
Interfere is getting in the way of a process; meddle is interfering in others' affairs without being asked.
Overt is done openly rather than secretly; transparent is open about how decisions are made, with nothing hidden.
Candor is frankness in saying what one thinks; veracity is truthfulness, the accuracy of what is said.
Guileless is free of deceit; ingenuous adds innocent trust, sometimes naive.
Hostile is openly unfriendly; antagonistic is actively working against, as antagonistic forces.
Antipathy is a deep dislike; animosity is active, lasting hostility.
Defensive is quick to guard against criticism; defiant is boldly refusing to obey.
Humble is modest about oneself; meek adds quiet submission, easily imposed on.
Unassuming is modest and quiet in manner; unpretentious is plain and down-to-earth, not trying to impress.
Impractical is not sensible or realistic; unworkable is unable to be carried out at all.
Ignorant is lacking knowledge; benighted is kept in ignorance, often by circumstances.
Connote is what a word suggests beyond its literal meaning; imply is what a speaker suggests without stating it.
Consequential is having significant effects; momentous is of great historical importance.
Noteworthy is worth noticing; significant is meaningful, having real effect or importance.
Profound is deep in meaning or effect; weighty is serious and important, as a weighty decision.
Augment is adding to the amount or size; enhance is improving the quality or the effect.
Revise is changing after review, possibly a great deal; refine is improving with small, precise changes.
Cite is quoting or naming a source as evidence; invoke is calling on an authority, a law or a principle for support.
Enumerate is listing items one by one; delineate is describing an outline or a boundary precisely.
Findings that conflict can't both hold; a person who contradicts states the opposite of what someone else said.
Controversial causes strong disagreement; divisive splits people into opposing camps, often by design.
A discrepancy is a mismatch between two things that should agree; an anomaly is one thing that breaks a pattern.
Inconsistent is not in agreement; incompatible is unable to exist together or both be true.
Discordant is clashing, as discordant voices; incongruous is out of place in its setting.
Incremental describes progress in small steps; cumulative describes the growing total those steps add up to.
Accumulate is gathering gradually into a pile or a total; proliferate is multiplying rapidly in number.
Nonchalant is coolly unbothered, often a pose; apathetic is truly lacking interest or concern.
Amateurish looks like a beginner's work; shoddy is badly made through carelessness.
Incompetent is lacking the skill a job needs; inept adds clumsiness in action, as an inept attempt.
Novice is the everyday word for a beginner; neophyte is a formal word for a newcomer, often to a belief or a field.
Mediocre is only average; second-rate is of clearly lower quality than the best.
Intensify is making something stronger; escalate is growing rapidly in stages, usually of a conflict or a cost.
Incite is stirring people to act; inflame is making feelings or a situation more heated.
Exacerbate means only make a problem worse; aggravate means that too, and in casual speech also means annoy.
Unfounded has no basis in fact from the start; untenable cannot be defended once challenged.
Implausible is hard to believe; preposterous is so absurd it is laughable.
Immaterial usually means beside the point; intangible means not physical, unable to be touched.
Irrelevant is unrelated to the question; inapplicable describes a rule or a method that does not apply to this case.
Digress is straying from the topic in speech or writing; deviate is departing from a norm, a plan or a path.
Benevolent is well-meaning and kindly, often of a powerful giver; compassionate is feeling for others' suffering.
Sympathetic is understanding someone's feelings; humane is treating people or animals without cruelty.
Meticulous is careful about details that matter; pedantic is fussy about minor details or rules, often to show off learning.
Cerebral is intellectual rather than emotional; erudite is deeply learned.
Temperate is moderate, not extreme, as a temperate climate; mellow is soft and relaxed, as mellow music.
A misconception is a mistaken belief; a fallacy is a flaw in reasoning.
Oblivious is unaware of what is happening; obtuse is slow to understand even when it is explained.
Bemused is puzzled, often mildly and with some detachment; perplexed is troubled by being unable to understand.
Moderate is not extreme in amount or view; temperate is self-restrained, or mild in climate.
Novel is new and different; unprecedented has never happened before at all.
Groundbreaking opens a new field or approach; seminal describes work that shaped much of what came after.
Disinterested is impartial, having nothing to gain; indifferent is not caring either way.
Blur is making less distinct, as a boundary; obscure is hiding, or making hard to see or understand.
Vague is not clearly expressed; nebulous is hazy and ill-defined at its core, as a nebulous concept.
Opaque is hard to see through or understand; cryptic is deliberately mysterious.
Redact is blacking out parts of a document; expunge is erasing something completely from a record.
Contest is formally challenging, as contesting a will; dispute is arguing that something is wrong.
Sequential is in a fixed order of any kind; chronological is in order of time.
Systematic follows a system or a plan; methodical adds careful, step-by-step habits, of a person.
Opulent is richly luxurious; ostentatious is showy in order to impress.
Elegant is graceful and refined; exquisite is extremely beautiful and delicately made.
Aesthetic concerns beauty and taste; an anesthetic dulls pain.
Candid is frank and honest; forthright adds directness, going straight to the point.
Selective is choosing carefully; discriminating adds good judgment of quality.
Passive does not act; complacent does not act because it is too satisfied to see danger.
Sluggish is slow-moving, of a person, a market or a stream; lethargic is lacking energy, of a living thing.
Dormant is inactive for a time, as a seed; torpid is sluggish and barely active, as an animal in the cold.
Tolerate is putting up with something; accommodate is making room for it or adjusting to it.
Authorize is giving official permission; endorse is publicly expressing approval.
Sanction is official approval given beforehand; condone is overlooking a wrong after it happens.
Persuasive is able to convince; compelling is so convincing, or so interesting, that it demands attention.
Unadorned is simply without decoration; austere is severely plain, even stern.
Whimsical is playfully fanciful, often charming; capricious is changing unpredictably on a whim, often a fault.
Playful is lighthearted fun; facetious is joking when seriousness is called for.
Humorous is funny in any way; witty is funny through clever use of words.
Divide is splitting in any way; polarize is splitting into two opposite extremes.
Provoke is stirring a reaction, often anger; antagonize is making someone hostile toward you.
Pragmatic is practical in approach and results-minded; utilitarian is designed for use rather than beauty.
Acclaim is public praise; notoriety is fame for something bad.
Praise is honest approval; flatter is excessive praise, often insincere, to win favor.
Initial is at the very beginning; preliminary comes before and prepares for the main event.
A predecessor held the same position earlier; a forerunner led the way to something that came after.
Prescient foresees events accurately; visionary imagines a bold future, accurate or not.
Retain is keeping possession of something; preserve is keeping it safe from harm or decay.
Recover is getting something back; salvage is rescuing it from wreck or ruin, often only in part.
Enact is passing a law; implement is putting it into effect.
Intermittent is stopping and starting; episodic comes in separate episodes, as a story told in installments.
Sporadic is scattered in time; isolated is a single case standing alone, not part of a pattern.
Sensible shows ordinary good sense; prudent is careful about risk and the future.
Rational is based on reason in general; reasoned is carefully worked out, as a reasoned argument.
Conciliatory is trying to make peace; appease is giving in to demands to keep the peace.
Balance is weighing competing demands against each other; reconcile is making them fit together.
Relevant is connected to the matter; pertinent is directly to the point at hand.
Apt means fitting, as an apt remark, but apt to means likely to, the way prone to does.
Germane is relevant to the discussion; applicable is able to be applied to the case.
Loath is unwilling to do something; averse is strongly opposed to it, as averse to risk.
Disinclined is mildly unwilling; reluctant is unwilling and slow to act.
Prominent is easily noticed or well known; eminent is distinguished and respected in a field.
Confine is keeping within physical or set limits; constrain is limiting the choices available.
Impose is putting a burden or a rule on others; enforce is making sure a rule is obeyed.
Restrict is limiting; prohibit is forbidding outright.
Prohibit is forbidding by rule; proscribe is forbidding by law, or condemning as harmful.
Encumber is weighing down with a burden; fetter is restraining as if with chains.
Severe is harsh; draconian is excessively harsh, far out of proportion, of laws or punishments.
Convey is communicating an idea or a feeling; disclose is making known something that was hidden.
Reveal is making known what was hidden; manifest is showing plainly, as symptoms manifest themselves.
Explicit is stated clearly in words; overt is done openly in action.
Unveil is showing publicly for the first time, as a new design; disclose is making known a fact that was private.
Sturdy is strongly built; hardy is tough enough to survive hard conditions, as hardy plants.
Immune is protected from a disease or an effect; impervious lets nothing through or is not affected at all.
Paucity is a smallness of number or amount; dearth is a lack, a shortage of what is needed.
Separate is dividing or setting apart; sever is cutting off completely, often suddenly.
Fragment is breaking into pieces; disintegrate is falling apart completely.
Measured is careful and deliberate; sober is serious and free of exaggeration, as a sober assessment.
Dignified is serious and self-respecting, a compliment; staid is sedate and unadventurous, often dull.
Equivalent is equal in value or meaning; interchangeable things can each be used in place of the other.
Duplicate is making an exact copy; replicate is repeating a study or a process to get the same result.
Similar is alike; analogous is alike in some respect that allows comparison, as the heart is analogous to a pump.
Mimic is copying someone's manner, often to mock; emulate is imitating someone admired to equal them.
A skeptic doubts claims until shown evidence; a cynic distrusts people's motives.
Wary is cautious about possible danger; leery adds suspicion of someone's intentions.
Marginal is small or at the edge, as a marginal gain; negligible is too small to matter at all.
The adjective slight means small or minor, but to slight someone is to snub them.
Minuscule and minute both mean extremely small, but minute also means attentive to the smallest detail, as a minute examination.
A premise is a statement an argument rests on; a hypothesis is an explanation to be tested.
Presume is taking for granted; presumptuous is overstepping one's place.
An inference follows from evidence; a conjecture is a guess made with little evidence.
Static is not moving or changing, a neutral fact; stagnant is not moving and going bad, a criticism.
Invariable never changes in practice, as an invariable routine; immutable cannot change by its nature, as immutable laws.
Terminate is ending, often abruptly or formally; conclude is bringing to a natural close.
Stringent is strict about standards; rigid is unbending, unable to adapt.
Resolute is firmly determined; steadfast adds steady loyalty over time.
Persistent keeps trying; tenacious holds on firmly and won't let go.
Subservient is too ready to obey, or ranked lower; servile is fawning and eager to please, always a fault.
Colossal is enormous in size; prodigious is impressively great, often of a talent or an effort.
Subtle is delicate and hard to notice, often of meaning; faint is barely perceptible, often of light, sound or a trace.
Abrupt is sudden and unexpected; instantaneous happens with no delay at all.
Cursory is quick and not thorough; superficial is only on the surface, missing depth.
Negligent is failing in a duty of care; remiss is mildly negligent, having failed to do what one should.
Superfluous is more than is needed; dispensable could be done without, though it may help.
Exceed is going beyond a limit or an amount; surpass is doing better than a rival or a record.
Impeccable is flawless; exemplary is good enough to serve as a model.
Bolster is propping up something weak, as bolstering morale; buttress is supporting an argument or a structure from outside.
Verify is checking whether something is true; confirm is showing that it is.
Defend is arguing against attack; justify is giving good reasons for.
Demonstrate is showing with evidence; establish is proving so firmly that it is accepted.
Evidence supports a claim; proof settles it.
Reinforce is strengthening an existing idea or structure; corroborate is confirming it with independent evidence.
Uphold is supporting a decision or a principle against challenge; sustain is keeping something going.
Validate is confirming as correct or acceptable; vindicate is clearing of blame or doubt.
Justify is giving reasons for; warrant is making something deserved or necessary, as results that warrant further study.
Smother is covering so completely that nothing can breathe or show; stifle is holding back, as a yawn or a debate.
Subdue is overpowering or quieting a person or a force; quell is putting an end to unrest or a fear.
Squelch is silencing, as a rumor or a protest; quash is crushing or canceling, as a verdict.
Startling is sudden and shocking; astonishing is so surprising it is hard to believe.
Thorough is complete and careful; exhaustive covers every possible part, leaving nothing out.
Painstaking is extremely careful, a compliment; laborious is requiring much hard work, often tedious.
Prosper is doing well, especially with money; thrive is growing strongly and healthily.
Blossom is beginning to develop and show promise; flourish is growing vigorously at its peak.
Opportune is well timed and favorable; expedient is convenient at the cost of principle.
Punctual is on time; prompt is done without delay.
Hasten is hurrying something along; expedite is speeding up a process by removing obstacles.
Momentary lasts a moment; fleeting passes quickly and can't be held, as a fleeting glimpse.
Transient passes through, of people as well as things; transitory is temporary by nature, of conditions.
Ephemeral lasts a short time; evanescent fades away as you watch, as mist does.
Trifling is small and unimportant; paltry is insultingly small.
Irrelevant has no bearing on the point; inconsequential bears on it but has little effect.
Authentic is proven to be what it claims, as an authentic painting; genuine is truly what it seems, including sincere feelings.
Typical is a usual example; quintessential is the perfect, purest example.
A precedent is an earlier case used as a guide; a paradigm is a model or a whole framework of thinking.
Ambiguous is open to more than one reading; inconclusive fails to settle a question.
