Perceive is noticing or understanding; grasp is understanding firmly, as grasping a concept.
Identify is recognizing and naming; discern is perceiving something hard to see, or a fine difference.
Insight is deep understanding of what is; foresight is wise planning for what will be.
Interpret is explaining what something means; infer is concluding what follows from evidence.
Perceptive notices and understands quickly; astute adds shrewd judgment of how to act, often for advantage.
Expertise is specialized knowledge; acumen is sharp practical judgment, as business acumen.
Homogeneous is the same throughout; monolithic adds massive and unbroken, often of an organization that resists change.
Anonymity is having one's name unknown; obscurity is being little known at all.
Uncelebrated is not publicly recognized; unsung adds that the recognition was deserved.
Diverge is moving apart from another path; deviate is departing from a norm or a set course.
Anomalous departs from an expected pattern, of data or events; eccentric is odd in behavior, of people.
Leverage is using an advantage to gain more; exploit is using for gain, often unfairly.
Utilize is putting to use; deploy is putting people or resources into position for use.
Vivid is bright and lifelike; graphic is vividly explicit, often of unpleasant detail.
Captivating charms and attracts; riveting grips attention so one can't look away.
Prices and temperatures fluctuate, rising and falling; a person vacillates, wavering between choices.
Vulnerable is open to harm; defenseless has no protection at all.
Squander is wasting carelessly; underutilize is using less than fully, leaving value unused.
Question is expressing doubt about; dispute is arguing that it is wrong.
Neutralize is canceling an effect by opposing it; negate is canceling out, or making invalid.
Query is asking for clarification or checking a detail; challenge is disputing the claim itself.
Counter is answering with an opposing point; rebut is answering with evidence meant to disprove.
Prevalent is widespread; commonplace is so common as to be ordinary and unremarkable.
Loquacious is very talkative, often pleasantly; garrulous is talkative to the point of annoyance, about trivial things.
Verbose is using too many words; prolix is tiresomely long, dragging on and on.
Fluent is speaking easily and well; voluble is speaking rapidly and at length.
Capacity is the ability or room one has now, as seating capacity; potential is what could develop later.
Context is the circumstances around a text or an event; subtext is the meaning beneath what is said.
Negligible is so small it can be ignored; insignificant lacks importance or meaning, whatever its size.
Intrinsic describes value or qualities belonging to the thing itself; inherent stresses a built-in, permanent trait, often a risk or a flaw.
Patronize is the act of talking down to someone as if helping them; condescending describes the superior attitude behind it.
Precede means come before; supersede means replace.
Precise describes a result or a statement exact in every detail; meticulous describes the careful person or work that produces it.
Protect is guarding from harm; insulate is shielding from outside effects, often by cutting off contact.
Interim fills the gap until something permanent arrives; provisional is accepted for now but subject to change.
Tentative is not yet definite, offered cautiously; inconclusive fails to settle the question.
Scarce is in short supply compared with need; meager describes a portion that is too little.
Conceal is hiding; suppress is keeping something from coming out or spreading, as suppressing evidence or a cough.
Apt is fitting and suitable in general; apposite is especially well suited to the point being made.
Celebrated means famous and admired; celebratory means marking an occasion with festivities.

Contend can mean compete, as to contend for a title; but contend also means argue a position (the authors contend that...) or struggle with a difficulty (contend with floods), which compete never means.
Contrast is any striking difference set side by side; disparity is a large, often unfair gap, as in pay or health.
Foresee is expecting what will happen; envision is picturing what could be.
Infrequent is not happening often; sporadic is happening at irregular, scattered times.
Misconstrue is taking someone's words or acts in the wrong sense; misinterpret is reading or explaining anything wrongly, as data.
Serene is untroubled calm; poised is calm and self-assured in action or in company.
Feasible is possible to do; practicable is possible to put into practice with the means at hand.
Dominant has the most power or influence; sovereign has supreme authority and answers to no outside power.
Minimize can be innocent or literal, as minimizing costs; trivialize is treating a serious matter as unimportant.
Ponder is the everyday word for weighing a question; cogitate is a formal, often humorous word for thinking hard.
A conspiracy is a secret plan to do harm; collusion is secret cooperation, often to cheat or deceive.
External is on the outside; extrinsic comes from outside and is not part of the thing's nature, as extrinsic rewards.
Barren is unable to produce at all, as barren land; fruitless is an effort that produced nothing.
Vain is useless or unsuccessful, as in a vain attempt; unavailing is the formal word, of efforts or appeals that achieve nothing.
Blend is mixing so the parts combine smoothly; fuse is joining so completely that they become one.
Naivety is innocence from inexperience; gullibility is readiness to be fooled.
Painless is without pain or difficulty; effortless needs no effort, often thanks to skill.
Profligate stresses reckless waste, often with loose morals too; prodigal stresses lavish spending, and can simply mean lavish, as prodigal of praise.
An aftermath is the period after a disaster; a repercussion is a later consequence of an action.
Analogous is comparable in some respect; akin is similar in nature, as if related.
Bona fide means genuine and in good faith, as a bona fide offer; authentic means proven to be the real thing.
A sanction is a penalty actually imposed; a deterrent is anything that discourages the act in advance.
A digression is a turn away from the main topic in speech or writing; a diversion is anything that draws attention away, or an amusement.
Validity is the soundness of an argument or a test; efficacy is the power to produce the intended effect, as a drug's efficacy.
To aspire is to hope to achieve something; an endeavor is a determined effort to do it.
Incremental is advancing in small added steps; evolutionary is changing gradually through development, as species do over time.
Substantial is considerable; immense is extremely large, far beyond considerable.
Tolerant accepts views or habits that differ; lenient is mild in punishing.
Stifle is holding back a reaction, such as a laugh; repress is keeping down by force, as a feeling or a people.
Grateful is thankful for a kindness; appreciative is also approving of quality, as an appreciative audience.
Laud is praising highly; celebrate is honoring with festivity or public praise.
Complicate is making a situation harder to deal with; exacerbate is making a bad situation worse.
Perplexed is puzzled and troubled; baffled is completely unable to understand.
Accurate means correct; precise means exact and detailed, which a wrong figure can also be.
An acute problem is severe and often sudden; a chronic one drags on for a long time.
Adequate means enough; abundant means more than enough.
Advance an idea means put it forward; advocate an idea means argue hard for it.
Affirm states a claim is true; assume accepts it without proof.
In careful writing, aggravate means worsen a problem; irritate means annoy a person.
Amiable describes a friendly person; amicable describes a friendly agreement or relationship.
Analyze examines details; summarize condenses the main points.
Arbitrary lacks a clear rule; deliberate is carefully chosen.
On the SAT, argue means make a reasoned case; quarrel means have an angry disagreement.
Articulate means put an idea into clear words; enunciate means pronounce words distinctly.
Assume takes something as true with no evidence; presume takes it as likely on some grounds.
Augment adds to something; aggravate makes a problem worse.
A bent is a natural inclination; an intent is a deliberate purpose.
Blasé means unimpressed from too much familiarity; nonchalant means calmly and casually unconcerned.
Blur obscures a distinction; blend combines elements.
Brazen means shameless; brash means hasty and loudly self-assertive.
Budding means just beginning; burgeoning means growing rapidly.
Cajole means win someone over with flattery; coerce means force them with threats.
Caution is care; censure is strong criticism.
Celebrate means praise or honor, often joyfully; commemorate means honor the memory of a past person or event.
Challenge questions a claim; refute proves it false.
Champion means actively fight for something; endorse means state approval of it, which takes far less effort.
Clandestine describes secret activity, often illicit; classified describes information a government officially restricts.
Coax means persuade gently; coerce means force with threats.
Coin a word means invent it; cite a word means quote someone else's use of it.
Collaboration is working together openly; collusion is working together secretly for a dishonest end.
Complex has many parts; complicated stresses difficulty in understanding.
Genial describes a cheerful person; congenial also describes company or a setting that suits you.
Consequent means caused by what came before; subsequent means simply coming after.
To contest is to formally dispute a claim or result; to protest is to voice an objection, often publicly.
Convoluted describes reasoning or structure that is hard to follow; contorted describes something twisted out of its normal shape.
Cordial means warmly polite; candid means frank, even at the cost of politeness.
Unproductive means achieving little; counterproductive means actually working against the goal.
Criticize finds fault; critique weighs strengths and weaknesses.
Cryptic means hiding its meaning; ambiguous means open to more than one meaning.
A skeptical person doubts a claim until shown evidence; a cynical person assumes the worst about people's motives.
Deep-rooted means firmly established over time; profound means intense or far-reaching in effect.
Demonstrate supports or shows a point; illustrate makes it clearer through an example.
Describe tells what something is like; explain tells how or why it happens.
Disparity is a gap between groups or amounts; discrepancy is a mismatch between things that should agree.
Dispatch is speed with efficiency; haste is speed that is often careless.
Divergent is a neutral word for differing; deviant describes departing from accepted norms, usually disapprovingly.
Downplay means make something seem less important; undermine means weaken it.
Draconian means cruelly harsh; stringent means strict, but not necessarily unfair.
Earnest stresses serious sincerity; honest stresses telling the truth.
Enhance improves quality; enlarge increases size.
Enthusiastic means eagerly interested; zealous means intensely, even fanatically, devoted.
Erudite means deeply learned; pedantic means showing off learning or fussing over minor rules.
Escalate means grow in size or intensity; accelerate means go faster.
Both can mean coming from outside, but extraneous stresses that something does not belong, while extrinsic stresses that it is not part of a thing's own nature.
Faithful can mean loyal, but said of a copy, translation, or account it means accurate.
Fervent is strong, sincere feeling; fanatical is extreme, unreasoning devotion.
Fluctuate changes up and down; flow moves continuously.
Focus means direct attention to a topic; fixate means be unable to stop attending to it.
Fundamental is essential; rudimentary is at an early basic stage.
Groundbreaking is an adjective for pioneering work; a breakthrough is the discovery itself.
Guarantee is an assurance or promise; a warranty is a formal product promise.
Hesitant describes reluctance to act; tentative describes a provisional claim or plan.
Highlight draws attention to something real; overstate makes it seem bigger than it is.
Hinder makes progress harder; prevent stops it from happening at all.
A hybrid blends two distinct kinds into one new thing; a composite is any whole built from separate parts.
Imply is what a speaker suggests; infer is what a reader concludes.
Indifferent means not caring about the outcome; impartial means caring but not taking sides.
Keen here means eager; acute means sharp or severe.
Lament expresses sorrow over a loss; deplore expresses strong disapproval of a wrong.
Lavish means costly or given in great amounts; luxuriant means growing thickly, like hair or plants.
Lenient is a deliberate choice to be merciful; lax is carelessness about enforcing rules at all.
To lobby is to press officials for a cause; to canvass is to go door to door asking ordinary people for votes or opinions.
Maintain keeps something in good condition; retain simply keeps possession of it.
Meticulous stresses care with small details; rigorous stresses strict standards of method.
To minimize is to play something down or cut it to the least possible; to diminish is simply to make or become smaller.
Mock means make fun of, sometimes by imitating; mimic means imitate, with or without scorn.
Mutual means each side gives to the other; common means shared by everyone in a group.
Myriad stresses a huge number; various stresses that the things are of different kinds.
Nascent has begun to develop; latent is not yet active.
Nebulous lacks shape; ambiguous has multiple meanings.
Negligible has little effect; subtle may matter.
Neutral avoids sides; indifferent lacks concern.
Neutralize removes an effect; moderate only reduces it.
Nonchalant describes a manner; indifferent means not caring.
Nostalgic longs fondly for the past; melancholy is sadness with no particular object.
Nourish supplies needs; nurture adds continuing care.
Novice lacks experience; naive suggests poor judgment.
Nuanced recognizes several distinctions; subtle may mark one.
Numerous counts items; voluminous describes bulk.
Objective follows evidence; neutral takes no side.
Obscure hides what is present; omit leaves it out.
Obsolete is superseded; archaic may still be used.
Onerous burdens; rigorous is exacting but may help.
Opaque blocks understanding; complex may still be clear.
Opportune concerns timing; convenient concerns ease.
Oppose works against; object may only express dissent.
Orthodox follows convention; original introduces new ideas.
Ostensible may hide reality; obvious is easy to see.
Outmoded is old-fashioned; obsolete is out of use.
Overlook fails to notice; omit leaves out of an account.
Overt is out in the open; obvious is easy to recognize.
Paradoxical only seems contradictory; impossible cannot occur.
Partial can mean incomplete; biased favors a side.
Peculiar is unusual; personal belongs to an individual.
Perceptive adds understanding; observant may only notice.
Peripheral is off-center; superficial lacks depth.
Perpetuate may keep harm going; preserve usually protects.
Pervasive reaches throughout; prevalent is merely common.
Pessimistic expects bad outcomes; skeptical doubts that a claim is true.
Pioneering stresses being the first to do something; novel stresses simply being new or unusual.
Plausible could be true; probable is likely true.
Polarize creates camps; contrast only marks differences.
Ponder implies sustained thought; wonder may be brief.
Pragmatic prioritizes workable action; practical can mean useful.
Presume accepts without proof; infer draws from evidence.
Proliferate increases rapidly; propagate actively reproduces or spreads.
Prolong lengthens duration; delay shifts a start or event later.
A proponent argues for an idea; a patron funds or protects it.
Protect shields from harm; preserve keeps a state intact.
Provisional remains until replaced; tentative is uncertain.
Prudent weighs risk; timid fears action even when safe.
Punctual meets a schedule; opportune arrives at a favorable moment.
Quash ends an effort; quiet may only reduce disturbance.
Quell stops disturbance; quiet may only reduce noise.
Query may challenge a claim; inquire merely seeks information.
Questionable invites doubt; uncertain may just be unresolved.
To rebut is to argue against a claim, while to refute is to prove it wrong; a rebuttal can fail.
Rectify fixes a fault; revise changes text whether faulty or not.
Refute shows falsity; dispute only challenges.
Reinforce adds support; repeat merely says again.
Relevant connects to the issue; significant may matter elsewhere.
Reluctant feels hesitation; resistant may actively oppose.
Render can make something become; depict represents it.
Repudiate means refuse to accept or be linked to; refute means prove wrong with evidence.
Rescind means cancel an official act, such as a law or offer; retract means take back a statement.
Resilient rebounds after stress; resistant may not be affected at all.
Reticent means unwilling to speak or reveal things; reluctant means unwilling to do something in general.
Revamp means rebuild thoroughly; revise means correct or change parts of something, such as a text.
Robust withstands stress; vigorous has energy or force.
Salient stands out in the argument; prominent may simply be visible.
Sarcastic remarks mock by saying the opposite of what is meant; sardonic humor is grimly mocking and need not reverse anything.
Scarce emphasizes inadequate supply; rare emphasizes infrequency.
Scrutinize examines closely; scan may be quick and broad.
Seminal shapes later work; original need only be new.
Separate parts things; distinguish notices differences.
Sequential stresses an ordered series; consecutive stresses no gaps.
Serene conveys peacefulness; placid may suggest little activity.
Severe marks harsh degree; stern describes a strict manner.
Shrewd has keen judgment; cunning adds crafty self-interest.
Significant matters; substantial concerns size or amount.
Similar shares features; identical matches exactly.
Simplify reduces complexity; summarize reduces length.
Slight is small; subtle is hard to notice but may be important.
Sober is measured; solemn has ceremonial gravity.
Somber means dark and sad; sober means serious and clear-headed, or not drunk.
Sovereign means holding supreme power with no authority above; autonomous means self-governing, possibly within a larger state.
Sparse describes spread or density; scarce describes availability.
Specific identifies a particular case; precise is exact in detail.
Speculate ventures beyond evidence; infer reasons from evidence.
Sporadic concerns timing; sparse concerns density or amount.
Spurious is false; specious looks convincing but is flawed.
Stable resists unwanted change; static does not change at all.
Stark adds harshness or bareness; striking only means it catches the eye.
Steadfast is loyal to a purpose; stubborn resists change regardless of merit.
Stem is checking a flow or spread, as stem the bleeding, often only slowing it; halt is bringing any motion or activity to a full stop.
Stifle restricts growth or expression; silence stops sound or speech.
Stingy means unwilling to spend, which is a criticism; thrifty means careful with money, which is a compliment.
Stipulate states a condition; suggest offers an idea.
Stymie means block progress; stifle means smother or hold back, as with a yawn or dissent.
Substantiate supplies evidence; illustrate provides an example.
Succinct is efficiently brief; terse can sound abrupt.
Sufficient meets a need; ample exceeds it comfortably.
Suggest hints or proposes; assert states with confidence.
Suppress holds down; repress often forces inward or conceals.
Sustain keeps going; support may only help at one point.
Sympathetic means caring about someone's trouble; empathetic means sharing their feelings as if they were your own.
Synthesize combines ideas; summarize condenses them.
Tax means make heavy demands on; vex means annoy.
To thwart is to stop a plan from succeeding at all; to hinder is only to slow it or make it harder.
Tolerate puts up with something; condone accepts a wrong as if it were acceptable.
Trivialize makes something seem petty or unworthy, a stronger charge; downplay only makes it seem smaller than it is.
Unambiguous means having only one possible meaning; unequivocal means stated firmly, leaving no doubt about one's position.
To utilize is simply to put something to use; to exploit can also mean to use it unfairly for one's own gain.
Validate confirms that a claim or choice is sound; verify checks that the facts are true.
Vehement means forceful in feeling; vitriolic means bitterly cruel and hateful.
Weighty in a text usually means serious and important; heavy usually means physically weighing a lot.
Moving means genuinely touching; mawkish means sentimental in a sickly, overdone way.
